title: Desktop Defender
genre: Desktop-companion idle auto-battler / omnidirectional idle shooter-defence that sits in a corner of your screen while you work (the 'desktop idle' trend of Rusty's Retirement and Bongo Cat)
release_date: 2025-11-04 (Steam, PC) [CONFIRMED – Steam store/Dekudeals; an earlier announcement said 2025-10-31; Automaton reports 5 Nov Japan time]
early_access_date: n/a (free demo; Steam Next Fest 2025-10-13 to 2025-10-20)
window_note: In window (Next Fest Oct 2025, release Nov 2025).
team_size: 1 [ESTIMATE – press consistently describes a single developer: Galaxus headline 'Der Walliser Game-Entwickler…' ('the Valais game developer'), Shazoo 'indie developer in shock', Mein-MMO quoting the developer's own X posts. No explicit headcount found; a publisher (Poysky Productions) is also involved]
country: Switzerland (canton of Valais/Wallis per Galaxus headline) [CONFIRMED – Mein-MMO 'small Swiss indie studio'; Valais from Galaxus]
developer_background: no data on prior games. Studio motto: making 'the games that nobody else makes' [press-kit wording via Mein-MMO]. Before Next Fest the demo had only ~3 concurrent players [CONFIRMED – developer on X, via Mein-MMO/Shazoo/Automaton].
business_model: Premium $4.99; launch discount 15% until 2025-11-19 [Automaton]; all-time low $3.49 (-30%) [Dekudeals]. Free demo kept online after Next Fest at Valve's encouragement.
units_or_downloads: No official sales figure found. Boxleiter: 1,770 reviews (~Sep 2026) × 50 (cheap <$10 idle game; mass-market buyers review less) ≈ 88,500 copies (range ×35–60: 62k–106k) [ESTIMATE]. Next Fest: ~20,000 wishlists gained during the October 2025 fest [ESTIMATE – How To Market A Game analysis]; one of the 50 most-played demos of the fest [CONFIRMED – developer via Mein-MMO].
peak_concurrent_players: Paid game: 2,673 all-time peak [ESTIMATE – SteamCharts]; monthly average 1,125 (Nov 2025) falling to 209 (Feb 2026); a later 30-day window showed an average of 458 / peak 1,112 [SteamCharts, dates approximate]. Demo: from ~3 to ~1,000 in 3 days, then 1,548 on 2025-10-18 [ESTIMATE – SteamDB via Mein-MMO/EGW]. For a desktop idle game, concurrent players are inflated because players leave it running.
steam_reviews: 1,770 reviews, 92% positive ('Very Positive'), ~Sep 2026 [Steam store snapshot]; earlier snapshots 1,319 (94%), 1,705 (92%), 1,746 (1,620 positive / 126 negative). Demo: 283 reviews, 98% positive.
gross_revenue: [ESTIMATE – Boxleiter] 62k–106k copies × ($4.99 × 0.75 ≈ $3.74) ≈ $230k–$400k Steam gross to ~Sep 2026; central ~$330k. No Gamalytic/Raijin figure was retrieved.
net_revenue: [ESTIMATE] gross × 0.70 × 0.93 ≈ $150k–$260k (central ~$215k) to developer + publisher; the Conradical/Poysky split is not disclosed.
production_cost: no data disclosed. [ESTIMATE] If one developer worked ~6–12 months at ~$6k/month (Switzerland is far above this; opportunity cost ≈ $8–10k/month), the cost is ≈ $36k–$72k at the spec rate, or $50k–$120k in Swiss opportunity cost. Publisher marketing spend unknown.
development_time: no data (announced July 2025, released Nov 2025; total development time not reported)
why_popular: Rides the 'desktop companion / idle-while-you-work' trend: a tiny always-on-top window in the screen corner where a turret auto-defends against waves while you work, study or stream. Zero-friction, low-attention, satisfying number-go-up progression. Very cheap ($4.99). Novelty of a game that 'lives on your desktop' is easy to show in a short clip. The Next Fest demo's jump from ~3 players to a top-50 demo produced press stories ('Valve wants the demo to stay') that compounded discovery. [Qualitative, from Mein-MMO, Automaton, Shazoo, EGW, Galaxus coverage]
marketing_channels: Steam Next Fest October 2025 (top-50 most-played demo, ~20k wishlists); demo kept live afterwards at Valve's suggestion; developer posting milestones on X, which was picked up by German, Japanese, Russian and Swiss press; publisher Poysky Productions (press release positioning it as 'Rusty's Retirement meets Tower Defense'); Steam 'More like this' for the desktop-idle cluster (Rusty's Retirement, Bongo Cat). Streamer/TikTok role not verified.
art_style: Minimal 2D pixel/vector art in a small transparent overlay strip; clean UI with upgrade panels
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the whole idle loop (waves, auto-targeting, upgrades, prestige, offline progress), save system, and the tricky platform bit, a transparent, always-on-top, click-through overlay window (Godot 4 per-pixel transparency / borderless window flags, or Unity + Win32 calls via Claude Code); generate small 2D sprites/icons (Retro Diffusion/Scenario), SFX (ElevenLabs) and lo-fi loops (Suno). | AI cannot: balance idle progression curves so they stay satisfying for weeks, judge how unobtrusive the overlay must be, nail the 'cozy but compulsive' feel through playtesting, or create the Next Fest/press momentum. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 (transparent window + always-on-top) + GodotSteam (achievements, Steam overlay), Retro Diffusion/Aseprite, ElevenLabs, Suno. Score 5: 2D, single-player, one core loop, small content.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: [ESTIMATE – spec method] 2–4 weeks, $120–$300 (Claude Pro/Max, image gen, audio subscriptions, $100 Steam Direct fee); excludes the developer's living costs
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: [ESTIMATE – spec method] 2–5 months, $1,000–$4,000 (subscriptions, optional pixel-art freelancer polish, multi-monitor/OS testing, Next Fest/press outreach budget); excludes the developer's living costs

data_conflicts: Release date: 2025-10-31 (July 2025 announcement) vs 2025-11-04 (Steam/Dekudeals) vs 5 Nov (Automaton, Japan time); 2025-11-04 is used. Genre label: 'idle auto-battler' (Mein-MMO/CogConnected) vs 'Rusty's Retirement meets Tower Defense' (publisher press release); both describe the same desktop idle defence loop. Team size is not explicitly stated; '1' is inferred from singular 'developer' wording in multiple outlets. Review counts vary by snapshot (1,319 → 1,770); the latest is used.
notes: This is the realistic end of the solo spectrum. It was not a mega-hit (≈ 60k–110k copies, ≈ $0.2–0.4M gross), but it is clearly profitable for one developer and is roughly in the top ~3–8% of Steam releases (see _market_stats.md: ~8% of 2025 releases grossed > $100k). The key lever was Next Fest timing plus a novel desktop-overlay hook; the demo went from ~3 players to a top-50 Next Fest demo, and the press picked up the 'tiny game, Valve noticed' story. Desktop-idle games keep long session times (players leave them running), which helps Steam visibility. Caveat: the market for this sub-genre is filling quickly after Rusty's Retirement, Bongo Cat and Desktop Defender.
